text:
sam: noticing packet drops and intermittent kube node heartbeats in east3a GPU pool, ~30% of pods showing NotReady. looks like a partial AZ network degradation. starting zonal evacuation.
anya: on it. which pools are affected?
mo hit: it's the gpu-rtx-32 pool in east3a, nodes node-e3a-gpu-{12..27} showing flaps. load balancer health checks failing intermittently.
leah: tagging ops-oncall. please post a short customer-facing note once we know impact.
ops-oncall: acknowledged. I'll publish to status page if we have sustained errors >10m.
sam: plan: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) drain workloads with `--force --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` for model-serving pods, 3) shift traffic to east3b/c and reserved dedicated capacity, 4) spin up replacement nodes in adjacent AZs if needed.
anya: doing step 1/2 now. command I ran: 
```
kubectl get nodes -l gce-zone=east3a -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}' | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl cordon {}
for n in node-e3a-gpu-12 node-e3a-gpu-13 node-e3a-gpu-14; do kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m || echo "drain-failed:$n"; done
```
mo hit: quick note — draining will push load to east3b which already has 80% pooled utilization for peak projects. consider bumping autoscaler or enabling burst from dedicated reserve.
leah: cost chat later — right now keep car on safety. ops-oncall can you increase LB weights to east3c and reserved cluster?
ops-oncall: increasing router weights: `traffic-router set-weight --region east3 --from east3a=0.1 --to east3b=0.6 --to east3c=0.3` applying now. expect 2-3m for propagation. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
infra-bot: Autoscaler triggered scale-up: requested 6 GPUs in east3c (request id: req-20260318-77).
anya: draining status: 8 pods failed to terminate due to local storage locks — working with teams to snapshot and force terminate non-critical stateful pods. posting list: model-embedder-v2, cache-writer, perf-bench-ctrl.
sam: if any model-serving pods cannot be safely moved, we'll activate the fallback model variant in hosted API for affected customers. prepping rollout: `api-rollout set-fallback --model rdx/ggml-7b-fp16`
mo hit: monitoring dashboards show 5xx rate for inference endpoints increased from 0.3% -> 1.8% in the last 6m. routing change looking effective, 5xx trending down.
leah: customer comms draft: "We're experiencing degraded capacity in one availability zone (east3a) affecting some low-latency inference. We're shifting traffic and have activated fallback capacity; customer impact should be limited. We'll update at 15m intervals." approve?
sam: approve, + please include link to status id: ST-4421.
ops-oncall: status page updated ST-4421. next update 15:30 UTC.
infra-bot: Evacuation progress: 12/16 nodes drained, 4 remaining (node-e3a-gpu-21..24), average drain time 6m.
anya: one node failing to drain due to kubelet stuck on image GC — will force reboot of node-e3a-gpu-23 to accelerate.
sam: go ahead. ensure the reboot uses the warm boot image with cached weights so model cold-start is minimized. annotate in ticket.
mo hit: forced reboot pushed, node back to NotReady -> Ready in ~2m, kubelet rejoined, pods rescheduled to east3c.
leah: are we still within SLOs for p50/p95 latency?
mo hit: p50 stable, p95 slightly elevated by ~90ms but returning to baseline after traffic shift.
ops-oncall: all nodes drained and cordoned. traffic fully shifted to east3b/east3c + reserved capacity. setting east3a to maintenance until further notice.
sam: great work. follow-up actions: 1) root cause triage for east3a network fabric (infra-ml + cloud provider team), 2) run a rebalance job to redistribute cached KV shards across AZs, 3) evaluate whether to expand reserved capacity during high-peak windows.
leah: assigning follow-ups: sam (rca owner), anya (rebalance script), mohit (scale policy review). I'll open a postmortem template and link ST-4421.
ops-oncall: closing incident in channel. final note: no customer-facing incidents recorded beyond transient error spikes; billing impact minimal due to reserved capacity absorb. :white_check_mark:
